A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FRABench/UFEval research. Their main text and complete appendices, including tables, figures and equations, support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v3.pdf reports original generalization evaluations, public-benchmark comparisons, multi-task ablations and supplementary 72B experiments.

after.justification: v4.pdf retains these original experiments and adds downstream DPO alignment results in Tables 6–7 and qualitative comparisons in Figure 31.

M1.justification: Section 4.5 and Appendix F add a downstream procedure that uses UFEval-generated preferences to DPO-tune LLaVA-Next-7B and SDXL-Turbo. This extends the application pipeline; the original evaluator's aspect taxonomy, pairwise assessment procedure, backbone and supervised training objective remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V4 substantially extends coverage from assessing evaluator judgments to training and evaluating downstream models for preference alignment. It introduces RLHF-V/LLaVA-RLHF training inputs and evaluations using MMHal, LLaVABen, LLaVABen.Wild and HPDv2, while repurposing Pick-a-Pic for alignment training. The original FRABench task and aspect coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The original evaluator comparisons retain their comparator sets. New Tables 6–7 compare UFEval-based DPO against unaligned base models, DPO using LLaVA-Critic preferences, and DPO using original Pick-a-Pic preferences. LLaVA-Critic's participation as an alignment-data baseline is new, although it already appeared as an evaluator comparator.

E3.justification: V4 introduces distinct downstream evaluation protocols: DPO training with 15k image-understanding and 14k image-generation preference samples, matched image-question inputs for the understanding comparison, and generation evaluation on 400 HPDv2 prompts using three quality scorers. These substantially extend the evaluation design. Existing FRABench splits, evaluator training settings and judge-agreement protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix I and Figure 31 add five qualitative image-generation comparisons between the base model, Pick-a-Pic-based DPO and UFEval-based DPO, examining visual quality and prompt fulfillment. Existing position-bias tests, aspect-diversity analyses, multi-task ablations and evaluator success/failure examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The three-annotator agreement reporting is retained unchanged, moving from v3 Tables 50–51 to v4 Tables 52–53. The new alignment results use the same single-score reporting practice.

E6.justification: The retained quantitative evaluator results match across versions. V4 adds substantive downstream findings: Table 6 reports MMHal scores of 2.41 versus 2.24 and LLaVABen.Wild scores of 61.4 versus 59.0 for UFEval-based versus LLaVA-Critic-based DPO. Table 7 reports HPSv2 scores of 29.9 versus 28.7 for UFEval-based versus Pick-a-Pic-based DPO. These are newly reported comparisons, not same-setting improvements over v3 results.

T1.justification: Appendix F adds mathematical formulations of the image-understanding and diffusion-model DPO objectives in Equations (1)–(2), with definitions of preference pairs, reference models and optimization parameters. V3 has no corresponding formalization. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: V3 presents preference-data generation for DPO as future work. V4's introduction, contribution statement and conclusion claim demonstrated value for downstream preference alignment. The central claims about unified evaluation, aspect generalization and multi-task synergy remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: V4 adds an explanation for excluding queries from universal-aspect annotation, interpretations of the DPO results, and diagnoses of retained failure examples in Appendix H. Some diagnoses are unsupported: the new attribution to 'poor math ability' accompanies a named-entity classification example in Table 71.

D1.justification: V4 documents hardware, batch sizes, optimization parameters and other settings for the new DPO experiments. It explicitly explains query omission for universal-aspect annotation, which was already reflected in v3's unchanged prompt templates. The separate dataset URL is replaced by a combined code-and-data GitHub footnote; this changes access instructions without establishing any availability change.

R1.justification: V4 adds references supporting the alignment application, including diffusion DPO, HPSv2, RLHF-V and LLaVA-related resources, while removing the Qwen2-VL reference. Table 1 expands positioning through aspect-count and generalizability comparisons. The main related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain largely intact.

P1.justification: The title now names FRABench, terminology shifts toward MLLM-as-a-Judge, and the abstract and introduction receive localized rewrites. Numbered subsections and appendix ordering are revised, and Appendix J adds a manuscript-writing LLM-use disclosure. Much of the original prose and narrative sequence is retained.

P2.justification: The document undergoes a substantial visual redesign from two-column main text to a single-column format, with widespread resizing, relocation and caption repositioning. Aspect-definition tables are regrouped, Table 1 gains aspect-count and generalizability columns, and Tables 6–7 plus Figure 31 introduce alignment displays. Most existing plots and table contents are retained.

improvement.justification: V4 turns v3's proposed future DPO application into evaluated image-understanding and generation use cases, adding practical validation and training details in Section 4.5 and Appendix F. This supports a limited overall improvement while preserving the original evidence. The gain is tempered by absent uncertainty estimates for the new results and unsupported additions to failure-case interpretation, particularly the 'poor math ability' explanation in Appendix H.
